fields.novelty_line: partly new. A self-over-other edge in predicting a model's own behaviour is in print only after fine-tuning (Binder et al. 2024, arXiv 2410.13787, ICLR 2025: Llama 70B predicted itself at 48.5% against GPT-4o's 31.8%, and untrained self-prediction was "weak"), while prompted tests find none (Song, Hu and Mahowald 2025, arXiv 2503.07513; Blandfort and Pawar 2026, arXiv 2609.09899: other models predict a target at least as well as it predicts itself, and first-person framing shifts reports 0.15 in the flattering direction against the same question about a generic agent). In people the same direction of asymmetry is well established, others judged more moved than oneself by an anchor (Wilson et al. 1996, J. Exp. Psychol. Gen. 125: 5.53 against 5.23 on a 9-point scale) and by media (Sun, Pan and Shen 2008, J. Communication 58: d = 0.646), but there the self-estimate is the one that errs (Pronin 2007, Trends Cogn. Sci. 11) or is no better than an observer's (Nisbett and Wilson 1977, Psychol. Rev. 84: subject and observer reports correlated .77 to .99). Ours is a prompt-only contrast on one model in which only the subject's name changes and the self label is the accurate one (Haiku block error 0.024 against 0.209, the Sam label over-predicting a pull that Kumaran et al. 2025, arXiv 2507.03120, show is specific to one's own answer: change of mind 13.1% shown against 32.5% hidden, and no difference when the answer is attributed to another LLM); no paper found states that, and Sonnet and Opus here are undetermined. Search: WebSearch and arXiv search (newest first) for "LLM self-prediction vs other-model prediction introspection", "self-prediction introspection language models", "anchoring self-report language model", "first-person versus third-person framing LLM self-prediction", "bias blind spot LLM", "third-person effect meta-analysis", "Wilson 1996 anchoring others more influenced"; arXiv abstract and HTML pages, the Sun et al. and Pronin 2007 PDFs, the Nisbett and Wilson scan, the readkong copy of Wilson et al. 1996; 2026-11-05. claude-opus-5-5.
